data.narrative:
Inari is a Series C robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $874.1M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer set of three same-stage, same-sector private companies (Hadrian, Agile Robots, Nimble Robotics) valued between $1.0B and $1.6B, alongside one public robotics comparator.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression methodology, using total capital raised as a proxy valuation base, applies a 1.7x multiplier typical of Series C advancement, yielding $1.5B. Peer-median analysis across the three identified comparables produces $1.0B, reflecting the midpoint valuation in the robotics manufacturing cohort. The peer range spans $1.0B to $1.6B, with Hadrian at the high end and both Agile Robots and Nimble Robotics at the median.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $850M to $1.7B, with a median point estimate of $1.2B. This median reflects equal weighting of the stage-progression and peer-median approaches. Key uncertainties include the relatively narrow peer sample (three companies) and reliance on disclosed valuations that may not reflect recent market conditions or Inari's specific growth trajectory. The $850M floor approximates the current capital base, while the $1.7B ceiling reflects stage-progression upside.
